reply.title: Squashing Values with the Logistic Curve
reply.story: When modeling processes where an input triggers a transition from zero to one, linear functions fail because they grow without bound. A curve that bends gracefully to cap outputs between zero and one is needed. By taking the reciprocal of one plus the exponential of negative input, we create a sigmoid shape that maps any real number into this bounded range. Adjusting the steepness lets us control how abruptly the transition occurs around the midpoint.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic function maps any real input into a bounded range between $0$ and $1$. Adjust the steepness parameter to see how quickly the transition happens.
reply.instructions: Adjust the steepness slider to change how fast the curve rises. Observe the output value update at the fixed marker.
